subject: Benchmark artifacts handshake & next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Gomez <qa+ops@fastretail.com>, Kevin Zhou <kevin@fastretail.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark artifacts handshake & next steps

Hi Elena / Kevin — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we can start a reproducible perf qualification run against the POC workload.

Summary from call:
- Target latency SLO: p95 <= 180ms for 512-token average response in the checkout flow (interactive API).
- Throughput target: sustained 250 rps with tail protection for spikes up to 400 rps for 60s.
- Streaming: must support chunked responses (1-2 tokens per chunk) for real-time UX; client uses SSE.
- Concurrency: ~40 concurrent users hitting the session pin pattern; KV cache warm-up expected.

What we're sharing in this thread:
- Prompt/seed set for qualification (attached): fastretail_prompt_set_v1.json
- Lightweight harness instructions (attached PDF) and a short README in Drive
- Measurement definitions: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, token-level cost, failed-request rate, and rebuffer events for streaming

Action items (proposal):
1) FastRetail: confirm the final prompt subset to use for the first run and mark any prompts that require redaction (PII).
2) Redwood: run an initial 1-hour soak at 200 rps to validate harness reproducibility, then tier up to 250 rps and run a 30-minute verification.
3) Both: enable sample logging and share a 48-hour window of synthetic request IDs so we can correlate traces.

Scheduling:
- Proposed first run window: Monday 2026-05-18 09:00–11:00 PT. If that doesn't work, suggest alternatives.

Notes on reproducibility:
- We will pin model hash and runtime config in the run manifest. Please provide any environment-specific headers (auth keys, session cookies) we should include in the harness.

Attachments: fastretail_prompt_set_v1.json, harness-instructions.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to getting this going.

—Priyom

Thanks Priyom — this is helpful. Quick answers inline and a couple of attachments.

- Prompt subset: attaching the annotated prompt set (fastretail_prompt_set_v1.json) with redaction flags on 3 prompts (cards ending in ***). We'll remove PII on our side but flagged for you.
- First run window: May 18 09:00 PT works for us. We'll have an ops engineer on the call to validate network egress rules.
- Streaming: our client uses SSE; yes, we can accept chunk sizes down to 1 token, but we measure UX rebuffer when cumulative chunk latency > 300ms.

Attachments included: fastretail_prompt_set_v1.json (annotated), run_auth_keys.txt (secure transfer via SFTP planned)

Two quick asks:
1) Can Redwood share the exact manifest fields you pin for reproducibility (model_hash, quant_config, batch_size, kernel_flags)?
2) Can you run the soak once with and once without KV cache warm (cold start) so we can compare tail behavior?

I'll loop Kevin for SFTP coordination.

Best,
Elena

On Fri, May 14, 2026 at 1:27 PM Elena Gomez <qa+ops@fastretail.com> wrote:
> Can Redwood share the exact manifest fields you pin for reproducibility (model_hash, quant_config, batch_size, kernel_flags)?

Yes — drafting the manifest template here (short form) and will add to Drive:
- model_name
- model_hash (SHA256)
- quantization: {type, bits}  <-- we include both software quant and kernel flags in plain text
- runtime: docker image + tag
- batch_size / max_context_length
- concurrency_limit / worker_threads
- prefix_cache_behavior (warm/cold)
- seed_prompts_file (versioned name)
- harness_version + harness_commit
- measurement-defs: what we measure and units (ms for pxx, rps, % fail)

About the cold/warm runs: we can do both in the same window. Proposed order: cold start (20 minutes ramp), steady soak (1 hour) with warm cache, then spike to 400 rps for 60s. We'll tag each sample with run_id and cache_state so you can filter.

I'll upload the manifest template and a short checklist to the Drive link in related_links. Marcus, can you confirm we have the SFTP plan for run_auth keys?

—Kimberly

Confirmed items:

- We will pin the following manifest keys in the run: model_hash, quant_config, batch_size, runtime_image, harness_commit, cache_state.
